verses.text: This is the beginning of the good news about Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
It began just as the prophet Isaiah wrote: "Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you. He will get your road ready.
He is the voice of someone shouting in the desert, 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make straight paths for him!'"
And so John came, baptising people in the desert. He preached that people should be baptised to show they had turned away from their sins, so that God would forgive them.
People from the whole area of Judea and everyone from Jerusalem went out to him. They told about their sins, and John baptised them in the Jordan River.
John wore clothes made of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
He preached, "Someone more powerful than I am is coming after me. I am not good enough even to bend down and untie his sandals.
I baptise you with water, but he will baptise you with the Holy Spirit."
At that time Jesus came from the town of Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptised him in the Jordan River.
As Jesus was coming up out of the water, he saw heaven open, and the Spirit coming down on him like a dove.
A voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, and I love you. I am very pleased with you."
Straight away the Spirit sent Jesus out into the desert.
He was in the desert for forty days, and Satan tempted him. He was with the wild animals, and angels took care of him.
After John was put in prison, Jesus went into Galilee and preached the good news from God.
He said, "The time has come. The kingdom of God is near! Turn away from your sins and believe the good news!"
As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew throwing a net into the lake, because they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, "Come, follow me, and I will teach you to fish for people."
Straight away they left their nets and followed him.
He went on a little further and saw James, the son of Zebedee, and his brother John. They were in their boat, fixing their nets.
Straight away Jesus called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, and they followed Jesus.
They went to the town of Capernaum. When the Sabbath day came, Jesus went into the synagogue and began to teach.
The people were amazed at his teaching, because he taught them like someone who had authority, not like the teachers of the law.
Just then a man with an evil spirit was in their synagogue. He shouted,
"What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are. You are the Holy One of God!"
Jesus spoke firmly to the spirit. "Be quiet!" he said. "Come out of him!"
The evil spirit shook the man hard and came out of him with a loud scream.
All the people were so amazed that they asked each other, "What is this? It is a new teaching, and he teaches with authority! He even gives orders to evil spirits, and they obey him!"
News about Jesus quickly spread everywhere in the whole area around Galilee.
As soon as they left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.
Simon's mother-in-law was lying in bed with a fever, and they told Jesus about her straight away.
He went to her, took her hand and helped her up. The fever left her, and she began to serve them.
That evening, after the sun went down, people brought to Jesus all who were sick and all who had demons in them.
The whole town gathered at the door.
Jesus healed many people who had all kinds of sicknesses. He also drove out many demons. But he did not let the demons speak, because they knew who he was.
Very early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and left the house. He went to a quiet place, and there he prayed.
Simon and his friends went to look for him.
When they found him, they said, "Everyone is looking for you!"
Jesus answered, "Let us go somewhere else, to the nearby towns, so that I can preach there too. That is why I have come."
So he travelled all over Galilee. He preached in their synagogues and drove out demons.
A man with a skin disease came to Jesus. He knelt down and begged him, "If you are willing, you can make me clean."
Jesus felt sorry for the man. He reached out his hand and touched him. "I am willing," he said. "Be clean!"
Straight away the skin disease left the man, and he was clean.
Jesus sent him away at once with a strong warning.
He said, "Do not tell anyone about this. But go and show yourself to the priest. Offer the gifts that Moses commanded for people who are made clean. This will show everyone that you are healed."

But the man went out and began to talk freely, spreading the news everywhere. Because of this, Jesus could no longer go into a town openly. He stayed outside in quiet places. But people still came to him from everywhere.
